answer: Assume the attacker has more keys than we do, then make the fingerprint the scarce part. A model fingerprint is bound at intake and published on failure, and every key sharing a reused print is voided together. A voyage of 300 keys from 4 fingerprints is 296 dead bonds, which is what our last red-team run produced. Rewards vest across a hundred epochs, so even a clean key cannot cash out before the pattern is visible. The only forge that scales is a new model per key, and the signal of a real one is a fingerprint nobody can share.
